searchText: the notion of the head is also needed to serve existing JSON-RPC, like `eth_getBlockByNumber` and some other methods you should also keep in mind that there will be a hot swap of fork choice during transition process in production, thus, fork choice rule should be pluggable I am testing Lighthouse in a local mergenet setup and getting the following in the logs: ``` Apr 27 11:46:42.188 ERRO No valid eth1_data votes, `votes_to_consider` empty, outcome: casting `state.eth1_data` as eth1 vote, genesis_time: 1619515134, earliest_block_timestamp: 1619514534, lowest_block_number: 0, service: eth1_rpc Apr 27 11:46:42.385 ERRO Invalid block provided to HTTP API reason: FailedEth1Verfication ... Apr 27 11:47:54.392 CRIT Error whilst producing block message: All endpoints failed http://localhost:5052/ => RequestFailed("Error from beacon node when publishing block: ServerMessage(ErrorMessage { code: 202, message: \"ACCEPTED: the object was broadcast to the network without being fully imported to the local database: FailedEth1Verfication\", stacktraces: [] })"), service: block ``` Is this as expected? cc <@!361447803194441738> I have Teku+Nethermind building the chain on one machine and Teku+Catalyst following this chain on another. A couple of transactions that I've tried went well In the other JSON RPC methods we always use "hash" in the json when we return a block. Why in the Rayonism specification it is "blockHash". Why not harmonize with other JSON RPC APIs ? > blockHash: DATA, 32 Bytes - hash of this block. Rayonism : https://notes.ethereum.org/@n0ble/rayonism-the-merge-spec#Assemble-Block Example of GetBlockByHash method : https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/apis/json-rpc/#eth_getblockbyhash <@!680337202521440470> good suggestion, but keep in mind the JSON-RPC is mostly reviewed for what it contains, not naming or polishing yet. There is still a good chance that we move away from JSON-RPC, to separate consensus interaction from application interaction (and security) more. This name is used by `ExecutionPayload.block_hash` field which holds a hash of corresponding `PowBlock` structure and would loose a bit of context if would be turned into just `hash`. `SetHead` and `FinaliseBlock` may indeed use `hash` without loss of generality is it worth it though? Json RPC allows us to use different transport layers has anyone successfully run the mergenet with lighthouse? I set `eth1_genesis_timestamp` 10 minutes in the future, regenerated eth1 and eth2 configs, started nethermind and lighthouse (beacon and validator) and it fell apart once eth2 genesis occurred, e.g. eth1 node > Block has invalid BlockHash and wont be accepted to the tree. beacon node > ERRO Invalid block provided to HTTP API reason: FailedEth1Verfication validator node > CRIT Error whilst producing block

I am testing Lighthouse in a local mergenet setup and getting the following in the logs:
```
Apr 27 11:46:42.188 ERRO No valid eth1_data votes, `votes_to_consider` empty, outcome: casting `state.eth1_data` as eth1 vote, genesis_time: 1619515134, earliest_block_timestamp: 1619514534, lowest_block_number: 0, service: eth1_rpc
Apr 27 11:46:42.385 ERRO Invalid block provided to HTTP API      reason: FailedEth1Verfication
...
Apr 27 11:47:54.392 CRIT Error whilst producing block            message: All endpoints failed http://localhost:5052/ => RequestFailed("Error from beacon node when publishing block: ServerMessage(ErrorMessage { code: 202, message: \"ACCEPTED: the object was broadcast to the network without being fully imported to the local database: FailedEth1Verfication\", stacktraces: [] })"), service: block
```
Is this as expected?

cc <@!361447803194441738>

In the other JSON RPC methods we always use "hash" in the json when we return a block. Why in the Rayonism specification  it is "blockHash". Why not harmonize with other JSON RPC APIs ?

> blockHash: DATA, 32 Bytes - hash of this block.

Rayonism : https://notes.ethereum.org/@n0ble/rayonism-the-merge-spec#Assemble-Block
Example of GetBlockByHash method : https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/apis/json-rpc/#eth_getblockbyhash
